explicit_limits: This is a dependency-free Dart 3.12 package baseline. It does not imply Flutter, web, build_runner, code generation, FFI, isolates, native assets, workspaces, or another framework/build profile.

Only .dart is source-inventory-owned. pubspec.yaml and pubspec.lock are project metadata, and analysis_options.yaml or build.yaml require separate configuration handling rather than source classification.

Dependency-free native test and smoke commands use direct dart <script.dart> execution. dart run performs implicit pub resolution in Dart 3.12 and writes .dart_tool plus pubspec.lock, so it is excluded from the read-only spine. dart test is conditional on a host-owned package:test dependency and lock state.

dart analyze and direct script execution must not run pub get, install packages, fetch dependencies, create .dart_tool, or create/change pubspec.lock. Format verification is check-only via --output=none --set-exit-if-changed.

The shared inventory classifies generated directories and generic generated-name markers. Common Dart units such as *.g.dart and *.freezed.dart remain source-classified outside those locations until the declarative profile schema owns language-specific generated globs.

The generic doctor proves pubspec.yaml presence, not manifest validity, and dart analyze 3.12 does not reject a malformed pubspec when analyzed Dart sources are otherwise valid. Pub commands can trigger implicit resolution and project writes, so a read-only manifest-validity gate remains pending.

The Dart SDK bundles analyzer and Analysis Server implementation, but this spine claims only native analyze diagnostics and project markers. Analysis Server protocol facts, analyzer API compatibility, resolved references/types, package graph completeness, generated sources, and SDK/API churn require separate version-gated evidence before a semantic outcome can be complete.
